newsitem.title: UK: BADMINTON-TOP SOUTH KOREAN PARK TO COACH IN ENGLAND.
newsitem.headline: BADMINTON-TOP SOUTH KOREAN PARK TO COACH IN ENGLAND.

text.p: English badminton pulled off a major coup on Monday with the announcement that one of the world's top doubles players, Park Joo-bong of South Korea, is to coach the country's top players from January 1997.
Park, a bigr name in the sport, has an initial contract which will take him up to the Sydney Olympics in 2000.

The South Korean will spend the majority of his time working on court with the country's Olympic players under the direction of Steve Baddeley, the Badminton Associaton of England's Director of Elite play.

Baddeley said on Monday: "To secure the services of the world's greatest doubles player will be of undoubted benefit to our top players. His level of expertise and experience and insight into winning major competitions is unique and could make the difference between a fourth place and a gold medal in Sydney."
Park. who is in his 30s, took some time off from the sport in recent years to finish a university course and is now a professor of sport science and management in South Korea.

But he returned to badminton earlier this year to take part in the Atalanta Olympics where he won a silver in the mixed doubles to add to a gold medal he captured in the doubles in Barcelona fours year previously.
During the period of his contract Park is expected to visit Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland to work with their top players as part of the British Olympic effort.
Despite high hopes of a medal or two in doubles competition at this year's Olympics, Britain returned empty handed after a disappointing tournament.
